Messages.Author: Phi
Messages.Body:
This question came up in a game I played recently, my Navar McLaren was
burned, can one of my opponents influence it later in the game and bring
it into play (if they have Navar in their deck also), it seems to me
a bit illogical, after all the vampire doesn´t exist anymore...

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <3o3epi$2...@driene.student.utwente.nl>,

Phi <baa...@cs.utwente.nl> wrote:
>This question came up in a game I played recently, my Navar McLaren was
>burned, can one of my opponents influence it later in the game and bring
>it into play (if they have Navar in their deck also), it seems to me
>a bit illogical, after all the vampire doesn´t exist anymore...

Illogical, perhaps. But it is a card game - and the intent is to remove
any consideration of the history of the state of the game -
the game state can be seen by looking at everyone's layout.

Burning a vampire (or any unique card) does not prohibit someone else
from controlling that same card later.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <3ogi8d$i...@newsbf02.news.aol.com>,


But it is not an effect on the burnt vampire. It is an effect on the
acting vampire (which is why it is an undirected action rather
than a directed one). The acting vampire chooses (names) a vampire
who cannot block the acting vampire for the remainder of the game.

If it was a directed action, I would agree with you - that it is burnt when
its target is. But it has no target (other than the acting vampire).

Tom?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie) writes:

>L. Scott Johnson <lsc...@crl.com> wrote:
>>Unfortunately Blood Bond is *not* played on a vmpire. It simply

>>Names a vampire. It is not burnt when the named vampire goes to the ashheap.

>Blood Bond does not instruct you to play it on a vampire, and therefore
>goes to the ash heap as soon as it is played. People typically leave the
>card in play as a reminder, but the card is not actually in play.

>Blood Bond names a given vampire card. If that vampire is burned, the
>Blood Bond effect ends. This may not be 100% realistic from a simulation
>standpoint, but it is how the game works.

If it names a particular vampire card, then why is it not a directed action.

This is equivalent to the effect of the Army of Rats. The Rats, though
not directed, affect only one Methuselah. If that Methuselah is ousted,
the Rats are not burned; they simply target the new Methuselah called
"prey".

Blood Bond chooses a vampire. If that vampire is burned, or is not yet
in play, the effect waits until a suitably named vampire enters play.

I would like to see a reason explain both the undirectnedness and the
targetted effect you propose at the same time.



Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
L. Scott Johnson <lsc...@crl.com> wrote:
>Unfortunately Blood Bond is *not* played on a vmpire. It simply
>Names a vampire. It is not burnt when the named vampire goes to the ashheap.

Blood Bond does not instruct you to play it on a vampire, and therefore
goes to the ash heap as soon as it is played. People typically leave the
card in play as a reminder, but the card is not actually in play.

Blood Bond names a given vampire card. If that vampire is burned, the
Blood Bond effect ends. This may not be 100% realistic from a simulation
standpoint, but it is how the game works.


